chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from Bakr ibn Ḥabīb, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the tashahhud, and he said: If it were obligatory upon the people as they say, they would have perished. The people only used to say the easiest of what they knew. When you praise Allah, it suffices you.

So the correct way to understand this report is that the negation of obligation is directed only to what exceeds the two testimonies, because that is recommended and not obligatory like the two testimonies. And what indicates that is:

key_terms.هَلَكُوا: they would have fallen into hardship or ruin

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum obligatory tashahhud in salat (prayer) according to this hadith from al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of tashahhud in salat (prayer), indicating that not every wording beyond the essential formula is obligatory. The concluding explanatory line clarifies that the negation of obligation applies to additions beyond the two testimonies, which are recommended rather than required.
